$comment: Configuration for Check-ReleaseDocs.ps1 (the release-docs drift reconciler).
Everything in this file is EDITORIAL DATA that cannot be inferred from git or GitHub.
That is the whole reason the file exists — see the notes on each section.
After cutting a release, clear 'acknowledgedCommits' — it is scoped to one cycle.
$comment_scopeAliases: Maps a conventional-commit scope to the phrases the release notes actually use for it.
Required because prose and scopes do not agree: scope 'datapad' is written 'Data pad',
scope 'cafind' is written 'CA Find'. Matching on the bare scope name alone produces
false 'undocumented' reports for entries that are in fact present.
Matching is case-insensitive and is done against ENTRY TITLES ONLY (### headings and
'- **bold**' lead-ins), never against body prose. That distinction is load-bearing: the
word 'compare' appears incidentally inside the CA Explorer entry's paragraph ('per-compare'),
so a body-text match would have reported CA Compare as documented while it had no entry.
Aliases are ORed. Give each scope every spelling the notes plausibly use for it.
$comment_ignoreScopes: Scopes that are never user-facing and so never need a release-note entry.
Commit TYPES chore/docs/test/ci/build/style/refactor are already excluded by type;
this list is for cases where the TYPE is feat/fix but the area genuinely ships nothing
a user would notice. Keep it short — every entry here is a hole in the gate.
$comment_authors: GitHub login -> the display name used in the 'Thanks' section.
NOT derivable from the GitHub API: login 'asantarelli' has profile name 'SDigitales'
but the notes credit 'Andrew Santarelli'; 'msarson' is credited 'Mark Sarson'.
This map is the attribution source of truth. An unmapped login is a hard error rather
than a guess, because silently crediting the wrong name is worse than failing loudly.
$comment_coveredOverrides: Escape hatch for a scope whose entry exists but whose title genuinely does not name it,
and where no honest alias would either. Prefer an in-README marker instead:
placed on its own line inside the Unreleased block. The marker travels WITH the entry, so
deleting the entry removes the claim; an override here survives the entry's deletion and
will then hide real drift. Use overrides sparingly and say why.
$comment_acknowledgedCommits: Full or abbreviated SHAs of commits the tool could not attribute to any scope (unprefixed
subjects) and that a human has decided need no release-note entry.
The tool deliberately does NOT guess for these. An unprefixed subject carries no scope and
no reliable keyword, so guessing would either invent drift or hide it. Listing the SHA is an
explicit human decision, recorded in the repo.
Scoped to one release cycle — clear this list when a version is cut.
